finding.evidence: The diff hardens `normalizeInlines` (packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:89) so `isStructuralInline` runs never merge, and its comment claims the rule matches "the paste path's `TextEditor.normalizeInlineList`" (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3820, which does have the guard). But `packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:992-1009` still merges on `inlineStylesEqual(last.style, inline.style)` alone, and it is the normalizer used by `Doc.mergeCells` (document.ts:891-893) when it concatenates the inlines of every selected cell's blocks into the top-left cell. `inlineStylesEqual` compares images by value (types.ts:497 `imageDataEqual`), so merging two cells that each hold the same image (copy/paste an image into two cells, then Merge cells) collapses them into a single 2-character run under one `style.image` — the second image is lost while offsets keep counting both, exactly the data loss the diff's new guard exists to prevent. verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as claimed. `Doc.normalizeInlinesArray` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:992-1009) merges adjacent inlines on `inlineStylesEqual` alone at line 999, with no `isStructuralInline` exception, unlike the two other copies of the rule that do have it (store/block-helpers.ts:96-98 and view/text-editor.ts:3820). `inlineStylesEqual` compares images by value (types.ts:497 -> imageDataEqual at types.ts:458-470), so two adjacent identical image inlines compare equal and are concatenated into one 2-character run under a single `style.image`, silently dropping the second image while offsets count both — the exact failure documented at types.ts:505-511 and guarded against in the diff. The path is reachable: document.ts:891-893 runs the normalizer over every block of the merged cell during `mergeCells`, which is invoked from the UI command `mergeTableCells` at view/editor.ts:3391-3396, and image inlines do occur inside table cells (view/table-renderer.ts:424-428). The all-empty fallback at document.ts:1006-1008 also retains `style.image`, whereas the new normalizer explicitly deletes it (block-helpers.ts:109-111) to avoid a ghost render. The only inaccuracy in the finding is the description of mergeCells as concatenating inlines across cells — it actually appends whole blocks (document.ts:868-881) — which narrows the trigger to identical adjacent images within one block but does not remove the defect. This is squarely in the blast-radius lane (a new guard with another entry point reaching the same mutation without it) and the impact is data loss, so it is blocking.

The cleanup writes also run after `consumePendingCursor()` was consumed by the type change, so they record no reversible presence (contrast the explicit `setCursorForHistory` at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1012-1019). verdict.reason: Verified independently and every element of the finding holds. `dropStaleStyleOff` builds an `edits` array and then loops `this.store.applyStyle(...)` per stale run (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:497-499), called from `setBlockType` immediately after `this.store.setBlockType(...)` (document.ts:539-544). The DocStore contract quoted is real and verbatim: store.ts:82-89 says to prefer `applyStyles` because "a loop of `applyStyle()` calls produces one undo unit per call on stores (like `YorkieDocStore`) whose undo granularity is tied to the write itself." On `YorkieDocStore`, `snapshot()` is a no-op (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2725-2727) and undo delegates to `doc.history.undo()` (2729-2734), while `setBlockType` (1461) and `applyStyle` (1763) each open their own `this.doc.update()` — so one block-type change becomes N+1 undo entries, and the first Cmd+Z restores only the dead flags. The batched alternative exists and is documented as one undo unit (applyStyles, 1786-1828). The path is reachable via `EditorAPI.setBlockType` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2802-2812, whose `docStore.snapshot()` is a no-op on Yorkie) and the heading shortcuts (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1063-1073). This exact failure mode is a documented prior regression in this repo (packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/editor-step-selection-font-size-undo.test.ts:13-23), including the note that MemDocStore-backed tests cannot detect it. In-lane for blast radius: it is a violated cross-module invariant/contract only visible by leaving the diff, impacting the YorkieDocStore consumer. No guard, transaction, or undo-grouping wrapper exists.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: `dropStaleStyleOff` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:474) has exactly one call site, packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:544 in `Doc.setBlockType`. `styleOffAsClear` (document.ts:431-458, line 452) does keep an explicit boolean `false` whenever the block's named style supplies the key, so that `false` is only meaningful while the named style keeps supplying it. The named-style layer can change independently of block type through EditorAPI.setDocStyles (editor.ts:2814-2821), updateStyleToMatch (editor.ts:2848-2853), resetNamedStyle (editor.ts:2855-2862) and resetAllNamedStyles (editor.ts:2863-2870); each calls docStore.* then only `doc.refresh()`. I followed those into both stores: MemDocStore (store/memory.ts:100-121) and YorkieDocStore.writeStylesAndRematerialize (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2684-2709) re-materialize block *spacing* only and never touch inline boolean styles. mergedFrom.summary: Format painter (Cmd+Shift+C / Cmd+Alt+V) silently loses its ability to REMOVE B/I/U/S now that toggle-off clears the key instead of storing `false`

finding.summary: Format painter (Cmd+Shift+C / Cmd+Alt+V) loses the ability to turn a flag OFF on the target, because source runs no longer carry an explicit `false`
finding.evidence: The painter snapshots the RAW run style at the caret — `this.styleBuffer = { ...this.getStyleAtCursor() }` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:869) — and applies it as a merge patch over the target runs (text-editor.ts:1013 → applyStyleToSelection → doc.applyInlineStyle). Previously a source run whose bold was toggled off stored `bold: false`, so painting onto a bold target merged false over true and de-bolded it. After `styleOffAsClear` the source run has no bold key, the buffer omits it, and the painted target keeps its bold — painted text no longer matches its source. Fix belongs in the painter (snapshot effective style, or fill absent boolean keys with `undefined`), not in `styleOffAsClear`.

verdict.reason: The finding's cited code does not exist. text-editor.ts:869 is the ArrowUp key handler, not the painter. The format-painter copy is text-editor.ts:909 `this.styleBuffer = this.captureFormatAtCursor();`, and captureFormatAtCursor (text-editor.ts:3009-3023) already does precisely what the finding asks for: it resolves each boolean against the effective style (`raw[key] ?? defaults[key]`, lines 3012-3013) and writes an explicit `true`/`false` for bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, superscript and subscript (3016-3021), so the buffer never omits a boolean key. On apply (text-editor.ts:1049-1053 -> Doc.applyInlineStyle, document.ts:397-402) that explicit `false` either survives as a named-style/link override (document.ts:452-453) or is rewritten to `undefined` by styleOffAsClear (document.ts:441-457), and store/block-helpers.ts:381-396 deletes keys whose patch value is `undefined` — both branches leave the target's flag off. Painting a non-bold source over bold text therefore still de-bolds it; the described regression is not present.

finding.summary: Named-style exception writes a real `false` that survives a block-type change / paste, re-creating the #749 dead flag outside the new guard
finding.evidence: `styleOffAsClear` (document.ts:394-418) deliberately KEEPS `italic: false` when the block's named style supplies the key (Heading 6). Nothing re-normalises that run when the block stops supplying it: `Doc.setBlockType` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:456) forwards straight to `store.setBlockType`, which only rewrites `type`/`headingLevel`/`listKind` and leaves `block.inlines` untouched — so Heading 6 → paragraph leaves an explicit `italic:false` in a paragraph whose style supplies nothing, i.e. exactly the dead flag the change exists to eliminate (unmergeable by `inlineStylesEqual`/`normalizeInlines`, and pinned against a later style redefinition). The same residue travels through the internal clipboard, which serialises whole `Block`s with run styles verbatim (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:10-23, 51-60) — copy Heading 6 text, paste into a paragraph, and the `false` lands there. Both paths bypass `Doc.applyInlineStyle`, the only place the demotion happens. Fix belongs either in `setBlockType`/paste normalisation or in a read-side rule that treats a false-with-no-supplying-style as clearable.

verdict.reason: Partially inaccurate but the core defect is real. The `setBlockType` half of the claim is refuted: `Doc.setBlockType` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:539-545) does not forward straight to the store — it calls `dropStaleStyleOff(blockId)` (document.ts:474-501) after refreshing, which strips exactly the `false` keys the new named style no longer supplies, so Heading 6 -> paragraph is handled. The paste half, however, is genuine and is a reachable bypass: `dropStaleStyleOff` has exactly one caller (document.ts:544). Copy clones run styles verbatim (view/text-editor.ts:3468-3474, 3491), `sanitizeInlineStyle` preserves an explicit boolean `false` (view/clipboard.ts:137-140), and `insertBlocks`' single-block branch splices the pasted inlines into the destination block and commits them through `updateBlockDirect` (view/text-editor.ts:3622-3635), which is a bare `store.updateBlock` + `refresh` (document.ts:566-569) with no re-normalisation. The premise holds too: `styleOffAsClear` keeps `italic:false` when the block style supplies it (document.ts:452) and `heading-6` supplies `italic: true` (model/named-styles.ts:91). So copying Heading 6 text and pasting into a paragraph deposits an `italic:false` in a block whose style supplies nothing — the dead flag (unmergeable under `inlineStylesEqual`, pinned against later style redefinition) the new rule exists to eliminate, reached without passing through `applyInlineStyle` or `dropStaleStyleOff`. That is squarely the blast-radius lane (a new guard with another entry point around it), so the finding is not refutable; only its `setBlockType` evidence is.

finding.summary: Hyperlink runs are a second place where an explicit `false` carries information, and `styleOffAsClear` does not exempt it — toggling underline off on a link is now a visual no-op.
finding.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/paint-layout.ts:387-391 renders `let showUnderline = style.underline ?? false; if (style.href) { ... if (style.underline === undefined) showUnderline = true; }`. So for a run with `href`, an ABSENT `underline` key means "paint the link default underline", and only an explicit `underline: false` suppresses it. `Doc.styleOffAsClear` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:398-417) preserves `false` only when the block's *named-style* defaults set the key (`resolveStyleInline(blockStyleId(block), ...)`); a hyperlink in a normal paragraph has no named-style underline, so the `false` is demoted to `undefined`. Result: selecting a link and toggling underline off (Cmd+U / toolbar U, whose write funnels through `Doc.applyInlineStyle`) now clears the key and paint-layout immediately re-applies the link's default underline — the user can no longer remove a link's underline, and the raw-style-based `getRangeStyleSummary` will report underline OFF while the canvas paints it ON (the exact toolbar/render disagreement issue #715 was about). The fix belongs on the new code: the exemption in `styleOffAsClear` needs to also keep `false` for `underline` when the slice being written carries `href` (or the paint default has to move into the resolved-style layer).

verdict.reason: The finding asserts that `Doc.styleOffAsClear` preserves a boolean `false` only when the block's named style supplies the key, and therefore demotes `underline: false` on a hyperlink run to `undefined`, making underline-off on a link a no-op. That is not the code present. `packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:452-453` has TWO exemptions in sequence: `if (defaults[key]) continue;` (named-style layer) and `if (key === 'underline' && block && rangeCarriesLink(block, from, to)) continue;` (hyperlink layer). `rangeCarriesLink` (document.ts:55-64) returns true when any inline overlapping/touching [from,to) has `style.href !== undefined`, so selecting a link and toggling underline off keeps the explicit `false`, which paint-layout.ts:397-401 honours (`style.underline === undefined` is the only condition that re-applies the link default). Both write funnels named in the finding pass the real slice offsets into this check: `applyInlineStyle` (document.ts:399) and `applyInlineStyleToCells` (document.ts:514). The companion cleanup `dropStaleStyleOff` carries the same exemption at document.ts:489 (`if (key === 'underline' && inline.style.href !== undefined) continue;`), so a block-type change cannot strand it either. The code comment at document.ts:415-429 documents both defaulting layers and the deliberate mixed-slice policy. The described condition does not exist in this repository.
